claims.text: Adaptive sampling or metadynamics can substantially reduce the cost of calculating fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The cost reduction would result from enhanced sampling efficiency in free-energy calculations.
The proposed method applies to elemental, binary, and multicomponent systems in solid and fluid states near phase transitions.
The intervention uses an adaptive sampling rate of 0.1.
The intervention uses a metadynamics bias factor of 2.0.
The proposed operating-temperature range is 1000–2000 K.
Modification or more efficient exploration of the free-energy landscape is the structural mediator.
Enhanced sampling permits accurate estimation of vibrational entropy.
Enhanced sampling permits accurate treatment of anharmonicity.
Enhanced sampling permits accurate treatment of electron–vibration coupling.
The proposed method would reduce computational cost by 50% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method would increase fidelity by 20% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method would be 30% faster than TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The proposed composition boundary is systems containing 2–10 components.
Accuracy may depend on the particular system and phase transition.
The adaptive sampling rate and metadynamics bias factor may require system-specific optimization.

contradictions.description: The material scope explicitly includes elemental systems, whereas the stated composition boundary of 2–10 components excludes one-component elemental systems.
